newsitem.title: USA: Merix sees Q3 loss, president resigns.
newsitem.headline: Merix sees Q3 loss, president resigns.

text.p: Merix Corp said Friday it expects that for its third fiscal quarter ending March 1, sales and net income will be below management's original expectations.

Merix said in a statement it expects sales will be about $36 million and it expects to report a net loss as high as $0.20 a share, adding that it hopes to return to profitability in its fourth quarter.
Merix reported profits of $0.55 cents a share, including a $0.03 per share gain in its 1996 third quarter on revenues of $46.9 million.

The company also said Larry Neitling, president and chief operating officer, has resigned to accept a business start-up opportunity. Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Debi Coleman will take on the title of president.

The company previously said it expected sales in its third fiscal quarter to be sequentially higher than second quarter sales of $35.8 million. The weak results were a result of lower gross margins of about 10 percent compared with 14.2 percent in the second quarter.

The decline in gross margin was due to higher labor and material costs coupled with higher expenses caused by the expansion of its sales organization. Third-quarter results are scheduled to be released on March 26, 1997.
"Although the adverse effect on third-quarter earnings is expected to be substantial we start next quarter with increased backlog and a better product profile," said Coleman.

"The company's goal is to be profitable in the fourth quarter of the fiscal year. While we are disappointed with current earnings, we believe this is a temporary situation and have taken the action necessary to support Merix's return to growth and profitability."
